dedupe_keys.name: national transport model ntm of great britain department for transport

description: The National Transport Model (NTM) is the Department for Transport's tool for estimating the effect of transport policies and forecasting assumptions on travel indicators such as traffic levels, congestion and vehicle emissions in Great Britain. Coverage: all modes; version 2 was updated to a 2015 base year with values of time from the WebTAG databook and trip characteristics from the National Travel Survey, Transport Statistics Great Britain, coach fares, the London road user charge, MOIRA rail model results and National Trip End Model v7.0. NTMv5 adds more spatial detail and is used to analyse national transport policy and roads strategy and to produce road traffic forecasts. Format and access: DfT publishes documentation, not the model: an implementation report and calibration and validation report (2018), an NTMv2R analytical review with stress tests and a backcast method, a peer review (2020) and an independent audit of NTMv5 (2021) whose corrections were implemented. Licence and cost: the model itself is not released. Caveats: outside users rely on DfT outputs. It is a reference for national network flow and capacity planning under policy and demand scenarios. It relates to the GB National Travel Survey, DfT road traffic counts and PTV Visum in the catalogue.
